doc.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Predicting the 2000 election and politicians serving business
summary: Predicts Republican defeat and says politicians must represent people; the world's pigmented majority changes everything.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: Okay, we have it on tape now.

They’re done. So whoever hears it here, they can harken back to that and see it. They killed themselves in the attempt to dislodge a duly elected president — on a scurrilous at best and morally filthy at worst — matter that they had no business spending such time, and money — $50 million, in excess of $50 million.
What kind of positive changes do you see, if that election goes the way you think it will, in our country? Or what do you think needs to be changed?

Well the people, the politicians sent to represent the people, have got to get back to representing the people and not the business entities that pay them. For them to sell their vote to the businesses and abrogate the promises to the people, that’s got to stop. That systematic betrayal of the trust of the people has got to stop. That has got to stop because we are now in a world where we are the minority. You see, as an American Negro person whose grandfather was a slave, I remember constantly being told that we are a minority and we have no power. But when you look at the world, only three tenths of the world’s population are unpigmented. Seven tenths of the world’s population are pigmented people. And in this so-called global society the once dominant force is now a minority force. And that’s got to change everything. We see it changing in our own country. You know, demographics have changed.
